verdict.rationale: The product documents its hardware: a $7 ESP32 board connected directly to the phone over USB-C, or through a Lightning to USB Camera Adapter, with the phone powering the board. It also has a flash.sh build/flash script and a four-step self-checking app setup. However, the evidence shows no itemized bill of materials, no exact board model, and no step-by-step flashing procedure beyond 'always build with flash.sh'. missing for 10: itemized BOM with specific ESP32 variant, detailed step-by-step flashing instructions (toolchain, ports, commands), explicit end-to-end bring-up walkthrough, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, hardware rigs come with a bill of materials, wiring, and flashing steps I can follow end to end

citations.quote: Let an AI model use a real iPhone with a $7 ESP32. Just the phone and the board: no computer, no jailbreak.
USB-C models plug in directly; Lightning models need a Lightning to USB Camera Adapter. The phone powers the board.
Always build with flash.sh: it applies the BLE buffer sizes in hardware/hid_bridge/nimble_cfg.h.
Setup walks through four steps and checks each one itself
